question: Assume an object of mass $2.22\text{ g}$ is placed $7.5\text{ mm}$ in front of a large plane mirror. Find the image position and the nature of the image formed.

State the fundamental laws of conservation of electric charges.
What will happened to a neutral body When it gains electrons?

What is Thermonuclear energy? What do you understand by the term reflection of light wave?

Assume the angle of minimum deviation for a prism of refractive index $1.75$ is equal to the angle of prism. Calculate the angle of prism, given that $\sin x = 2\sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$.

Consider an astronomical telescope with an objective of focal length $108\text{ cm}$ and an eyepiece of focal length $7\text{ cm}$. if the telescope is in its normal adjustment, calculate the angular magnification (magnifying power), the distance of the eye-ring from the eyepiece and the diameter of the eye-ring if the objective diameter is $50\text{ mm}$.

If an object of mass $3.21\text{ kg}$ is placed $14.73\text{ cm}$ in front of a very long plane mirror. Find the nature of the image formed and the magnification produced.

Calculate the e.m.f. induced in a coil of inductance $12\text{ H}$ by a current changing at the rate of $2.7\text{ A/s}$.
Briefly explain the following terms: magnetic flux and magnetic flux density, Electromotive force (emf) and Magnetomotive force (mmf).

Find the values of temperature coefficient of resistance, its resistance at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and its resistivity at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $20^\circ\text{C}$.
Briefly explain the following terms, (how are they connected in a given circuit): galvanometer, voltmeter, ammeter.

Calculate the induced e.m.f. in a coil of $200\text{ turns}$ when there is a change of flux of $0.025\text{ Wb}$ linking with it in $0.50\text{ seconds}$.

Calculate: (i) the impedance and current flowing in the circuit. Is the circuit inductive or capacitive? State your reason. (ii) The phase difference between the supply voltage and current, (iii) The resonant frequency.
State and briefly discuss the four methods in which electrons can be ejected out of a metal surface.

The equation for the energy of the nth state ($E_n$) of the electron in the hydrogen atom can be expressed (in eV) as: $E_n = -\frac{me^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^2 n^2}$. By substituting the values of the constants, find the value of $E_n$ (in eV) in terms of $n$. what is name given to $n$ in this equation? Hence, find the value of $E_4 - E_1$.

From a sodium surface, light of wavelength $3125\text{ \AA}$ and $3650\text{ \AA}$ causes emission of electrons whose maximum kinetic energy is $2.128\text{ eV}$ and $1.595\text{ eV}$, respectively. Use these information to determine Planck's constant and the work function of sodium.
